Six comments

A Birthday Polka

Composed by Jim Murray, from a Sharon Shannon track.

↳ Posted by birlibirdie on November 30th, 2010.

This is not the original version as heard on the said track since the final cadence to DMaj “…|Ad c^/d/e|d4||”, or something like that, irritaded me! Sorry! ;- )

↳ Posted by birlibirdie on November 30th, 2010.

A Birthday Polka… for Pauline?

The 1st part of this polka sounds very much like the 2nd part of
La Pauline, a Contredanse from Normandy:
dG ge|de/d/ cB|AD Ad|BG GD|
BG ge|de/d/ cB|AD AB|1 G3 D:|2 (G2 G/)A/B/A/||
Is this coincidental?

The first part of La Pauline is different enough to warrant further comparison:
X: 1
T: La Pauline
M: 2/4
L: 1/8
R: Contredanse
K: Cmaj
ce ce|dd/c/ dd/e/|ff/e/ fa|g2 ee|
ce ce|dd/c/ dd/e/|fa/g/ fB|1 c3 c/G/:|2 c2 Ge||
K: Gmaj
dG ge|de/d/ cB|AD Ad|BG GD|
BG ge|de/d/ cB|AD AB|1 G3 D:|2 (G2 G/)A/B/A/||

there’s a version of this ‘contradanse’ at:
http://www.mustradlib.net/ (To get there, click on ‘La Musique’ in the list on the left, then on ‘Les Partitions’ and ‘Les Airs’ and select ‘Normandie’ on the right panel.)
